Good afternoon. Pavel, from Kazan. So, what did you find?
Dejair, from Brazil. Our main finding is that the pain continues after the infection is treated.
And before you ask: our sample is small. Sixty patients, in three centres.
Thank you for saying that first. Not everybody does. How long did you follow them?
Two years, but only forty-one of them. Eighteen per cent stopped before the end.
And the pain scores?
They decreased in most of that group, and increased in a few. The difference is significant, but with sixty patients I would rather say the treatment helps many patients than say it works.
That is a careful way to put it. Do you have much data on the first three months?
No, and that is our real limitation. The pain diaries came back incomplete.
We had the same problem. We solved it with phone calls instead of diaries. I will send you the protocol.

A short warning before you present your numbers this week. In English, the word significant does not mean big. It means the difference is probably not chance. So a very small difference can be significant, and a very large difference in twelve patients may not be. Please do not say significant when you mean important, because half the room will hear a statistical claim you did not intend to make. If you mean it matters to the patient, say it matters to the patient. And one more thing. When you have few patients, say so early and say it yourself. If the audience finds it, it becomes a weakness. If you say it first, it becomes honesty.

Our sample was small. Sixty patients, and I will say that at the beginning so nobody has to ask. We do not have much data on the first three months, because the pain diaries came back incomplete, and that is a real limitation. What we do have is two years of follow-up on forty-one of them. Pain scores decreased in most of that group, and increased in a few, and the difference is significant. But I would rather say the treatment helps many patients than say it works, because we still do not know which patients, and that is the question I brought to this congress.
